nodes.name: infra
nodes.en: The infra compose stack: the substrate every other stack leans on — the edge proxy, the identity provider, the secret vault, and the shared relational and key-value stores. Nothing here is a destination in its own right; the things here are what make the rest possible.

nodes.name: authentik
nodes.en: Authentik, the identity provider that decides who a request belongs to. It issues OIDC tokens and proxy headers for every other system, holds the group memberships that drive access tiers, and is the only place a person actually types a password.

nodes.name: authentik-credential
nodes.en: The Authentik API token. An issued administrative secret scoped to the identity provider itself: it authorises reads and writes of users, groups, providers and flows, and rotating it changes nothing about who can log in.

nodes.name: bluesky-pds
nodes.en: The Bluesky Personal Data Server, an AT Protocol repository host. It owns social handles and their signed record repositories, which is a different kind of account from the OIDC login used everywhere else on the estate.

nodes.name: bluesky-pds-credential
nodes.en: The AT Protocol session token held for a repository account. A short-lived bearer credential minted by a handle-and-password exchange, unlike the long-lived API tokens issued elsewhere on the estate.

nodes.name: infisical
nodes.en: Infisical, the machine-facing secret vault. Infrastructure credentials are stored, versioned and fetched here by the playbook and by agents over an API — distinct from the personal password manager, which is for humans.

nodes.name: infisical-credential
nodes.en: The Infisical service token. An issued secret whose only purpose is to fetch other secrets, scoped to one project path; it sits at the root of the estate's secret chain.

nodes.name: mariadb
nodes.en: MariaDB, the second relational engine, kept because several PHP applications ship MySQL-dialect schemas and migrations that PostgreSQL will not accept. It is a compatibility store, not the preferred one.

nodes.name: portainer
nodes.en: Portainer, the browser console over the Docker daemon. It inspects containers, images, volumes and logs across every compose stack without an SSH session.

nodes.name: portainer-credential
nodes.en: The Portainer bearer token. A short-lived secret minted by an authentication call, granting whatever the container console itself can do — which is broad, because that console reaches the Docker daemon.

nodes.name: postgresql
nodes.en: PostgreSQL, the estate's shared relational OLTP store. Services that need transactions, joins and a SQL schema keep their durable rows here — as opposed to the in-memory cache beside it, which keeps nothing.

nodes.name: redis
nodes.en: Redis, the shared in-memory key-value store. It holds sessions, locks, hot lookups and worker queues; everything in it is expendable and nothing is expected to survive a restart.

nodes.name: smtp-stalwart
nodes.en: Stalwart, the estate's real mail server: SMTP submission and delivery plus IMAP and JMAP mailboxes. Outbound notifications and per-user mailboxes both terminate here, unlike the capture-only development trap.

nodes.name: traefik
nodes.en: Traefik, the edge proxy. It terminates TLS and maps each hostname to a container; every request from outside the estate enters here first, and this is where the forward-auth identity check is attached.
